caption: One wavelength λ is the distance the wave travels in one cycle, marked here crest to crest. The pool's own shortcut: wavelength in meters equals 300 divided by frequency in megahertz — at 146 MHz, λ = 300 / 146 ≈ 2 m, which is why it is called the 2-meter band. (The 300 comes from the wave's speed, about 3×10⁸ m/s; higher frequency means shorter wavelength.)
